statement: Pedro must choose two irreducible fractions with positive numerator and denominator summing to 2, with numerator sum equal to 1000. How many ways can he do this?

44 points on a line numbered 1–44 left-to-right. Crickets start at 1 and jump to 44; each jump goes from a smaller to a larger numbered point. For every pair $i < j$, some cricket jumps directly from $i$ to $j$. Find the minimum number of crickets needed.

Cutting a convex $n$-gon: choose two consecutive sides $AB$, $BC$; replace them by $AM$, $MN$, $NC$ (midpoints). Start with regular hexagon $P_6$ of area 1 and cut repeatedly. Prove the area of $P_n$ is always $> 2/3$.
Pablo writes integers on a $2010 \times 2010$ board. Silvia can add 1 to each of the three cells of any L-tromino. Prove Silvia can always make all entries divisible by 10.

The incircle of $\triangle ABC$ touches $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$. Let $\omega_a$, $\omega_b$, $\omega_c$ be the circumcircles of $\triangle EAF$, $\triangle DBF$, $\triangle DCE$. Lines $DE$ and $DF$ meet $\omega_a$ again at $E_a$, $F_a$; define $r_A = E_a F_a$, $r_B$, $r_C$ analogously. Show $r_A$, $r_B$, $r_C$ form a triangle with vertices on the sides of $\triangle ABC$.
Does there exist an infinite sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots$ of nonneg­ative integers in which every nonneg­ative integer appears exactly once and $b_n = a_n + n$ gives all primes each exactly once?
